title: Request-slicing for rerank endpoint to cut tail latency and enforce token budgets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Customers using the rerank endpoint report high p99 tail latency on long-candidate lists and variable latency when candidate lengths vary. Current single-threaded per-request processing causes head-of-line blocking in our serving runtime when large candidate sequences are present. Goal: reduce p95/p99 latency by 30–50% for typical rerank workloads (candidate counts 8–128, token budgets up to 4096) while preserving or improving ranking quality (MRR/NDCG). Constraints: must remain compatible with existing API surface, not increase cost per token materially, avoid large changes to model binaries, and keep fallback path for older Dedicated/private deployments.

Proposed approach (request-slicing):
- Slice incoming rerank requests into smaller sub-batches ("slices") of candidates (configurable slice_size, default 8) processed in parallel across worker threads/replicas.
- Enforce a per-request token_budget and per-candidate token_cap to limit worst-case KV cache growth and per-slice work.
- Use an asynchronous merge phase that aggregates logits/scores from slices and computes final ranking; merge is CPU-only and lightweight.
- Maintain KV cache reuse within a request by sharing prefix caches across slices where prefix overlap exists; fallback to cold eval for completely disjoint candidates.
- Add adaptive timeout per-slice (based on historical per-model p50/p95 latency for the slice token length) and hedging: if a slice misses its timeout, trigger a speculative execution on a spare worker with aggressive token_cap.
- Add admission control that converts very long candidate lists into staged responses: return partial ranking quickly (top K stable) and stream full ranking when ready.

Implementation notes:
- Runtime changes primarily in rerank request dispatcher and scheduler. Minimal changes to model execution kernel; add API hook to support token_cap parameter.
- New config flags: rerank.slice_size, rerank.slice_timeout_ms, rerank.token_cap_ratio, rerank.partial_stream_threshold.
- Metric instrumentation: per-slice latency, slice_retries, hedged_executions, merge_time, per-request token_count, MRR delta vs baseline.

Why different from previous work: Instead of purely parallelizing at the token-level or increasing global concurrency, request-slicing targets the unit of independent candidate scoring while bounding token work per slice. This avoids long tail caused by a few large candidates and allows predictable per-request resource planning.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency for rerank (8–64 candidates) improves by >=30% in staging load tests compared to baseline (runtime-1.24)
p99 latency improves by >=20% for median workloads without increasing median cost/token by >5%
No regression in ranking quality: MRR change <= -0.5% on standard eval suite (rerank-2026-eval) and NDCG within 1%
Feature controlled by runtime flags and can be disabled at request-level
Canary rollout path exists with automatic fallback to legacy behavior on error or quality regression
progress_updates: 2026-02-21: Spike complete — microbenchmarks show 25–40% p95 improvement for synthetic workloads when slice_size=8. Observed small MRR delta (~0.2%) on WYSIWYG prompt set.
2026-02-26: Implemented prototype dispatcher and slice-merger. KV cache sharing API added in runtime (PR 4523). Initial unit tests and integration tests added.
2026-03-03: Load test in staging with 50% traffic pattern (mix of short and long candidates) — p95 improved 32%, p99 improved 18%, hedging triggered in 3% of requests and reduced tail by 12%.
2026-03-08: Design review with PM and SRE. Action items: tighten per-slice default timeout, add circuit-breaker for hedging storms, and prepare canary dashboard panels.
2026-03-10: Security review triage: token_cap is a runtime tuning knob; product reviewed and marked no additional cryptographic concerns. Security review required: false
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for slice dispatcher, merge correctness, and token_budget enforcement. 2) Integration tests that validate ranking equivalence across slice_size values on rerank-2026-eval dataset. 3) Staging soak with synthetic traffic at 2x expected QPS for 24h, measure p50/p95/p99 and MRR. 4) Canary rollout to 5% traffic with realtime quality monitoring and automatic rollback if MRR delta < -1% or p99 increases.
rollout_plan: - Feature gated behind runtime flag and API parameter. - Canary to 5% of Hosted API traffic for 24h. Monitor rerank_p99, rerank_mrr_delta, hedged_executions. - If stable, expand to 25% for 48h, then 100% for Hosted API. - For Dedicated and Private customers, publish opt-in runtime config and migration guide; do not enable by default until 2-week opt-in window and compatibility checks complete.
risks: Hedging can increase GPU usage under pathological traffic and cause capacity churn if not throttled
Subtle ranking differences if token_cap truncates context for long candidates — mitigated by per-candidate cap tuning and eval suite
Interference with KV cache eviction policies leading to higher churn if many unique prefixes are processed in parallel
